messages:
maya: noticing hosted p95/p99 spike starting ~09:12 UTC, user-visible latency up ~2.3x. graphs: <https://grafana.redwood/hosted/latency?from=2026-03-18T09:00&to=2026-03-18T09:20> :eyes:
liam: on it. do we have service-level breakdown? per-route or global?
maya: looks global across text-generation routes, but most pronounced on short-request routes (<=64 tokens). p99 for /v1/generate from 120ms -> 380ms.
raj: any recent deploys around 09:10-09:15?
deploy-bot: Deployment completed: kernel-selection v3.1 rolled to hosted pool at 2026-03-18T09:11:23Z by eva. changelog: reverted fallback heuristics -> new batch packing.
liam: good catch, tie in timeline to deploy. can we get queue depth and rate-limiter logs?
maya: pulling traces. queue depth on worker-pool-3 jumped from 2->18 concurrent requests, backlog ~350 req/s for ~40s. rate limiter shows a single tenant hitting 1.2k rps at 09:11:40.
eva: single tenant burst, likely PLG usage spike. but why p99 so bad for small requests?
raj: my hunch: kernel-selection change made small requests prefer the large-seq kernel path (higher per-request kernel startup). also packing window reduced, causing more micro-batches (worse latency).
liam: can we repro locally? maya, can you paste example curl for typical short request?
maya: sample request from logs:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hi","max_tokens":16}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
```
liam: repro script running with 100 rps for small payloads. observed increased kernel load and >2x tail.
raj: profiler dump from one runtime instance during spike:
```
PROFILE SUMMARY (worker-pool-3)
CPU: user 34% sys 12%
GPU kernels: small-seq-kernel (invocations 2100, avg 0.9ms), large-seq-kernel (invocations 420, avg 6.4ms)
KV cache ops: hits 78%, misses 22% -> extra KV lookups increasing latency
Batch sizes: median 1, mean 1.9, 95th 5
```
maya: median batch size of 1 for short requests, so batching not helping. kernel-selection moved some small requests to large-seq kernel (see invocations).
eva: so change in selection + bursty tenant = micro-batches + wrong kernel path -> tail latency.
liam: temporary mitigation: throttle tenant burst or apply per-tenant burst limiter. can ops throttle?
maya: can apply soft throttle at ingress for that tenant within 2 minutes. will do now.
ops-bot: Rate limit applied: tenant=tenant_42, policy=soft_burst_block, limit=800 rps, started 2026-03-18T09:14:05Z.
liam: after throttle, p95 back to baseline, p99 improving but still ~1.3x for a bit. traces show KV cache churn: prefix mismatch during burst -> misses.
raj: follow-up: revert kernel-selection heuristic or fix mapping so short sequences use the small-seq optimized kernel. Also increase batching window slightly when median batch size < 2 to try to pack micros.
maya: i ran A/B on small subset: reverting kernel-selection for hosted pool -> tail latency returns to normal within 30s.
deploy-bot: Rollback executed: kernel-selection v3.1 -> v3.0 on pool hosted-1 at 2026-03-18T09:16:40Z by raj.
liam: nice. action items: 1) make kernel-selection safer (feature gate + canary on low-burst tenants), 2) improve batching heuristics to avoid micro-batch path for short payload bursts, 3) KV cache prefix normalization to reduce churn, 4) add tenant burst detection alert and auto-soft-throttle.
eva: i'll open tickets and drive prioritization with product.
raj: i'll follow up with a perf PR that adds a conservative fallback when median batch size < 2 and a knob to force small-seq kernel for requests <=64 tokens.
maya: leaving traces and profiler logs in drive: <https://drive.redwood/reports/1813456789-hosted-latency-spike>
liam: marking incident as mitigated, keeping watch for 1hr. thanks all. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — will keep an eye on KV miss rate and batch sizes.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring (2026-03-18T09:18:00Z).
